newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spot Prods - NYH quiet, Gulf premium soft.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spot Prods - NYH quiet, Gulf premium soft.

text.p: U.S. spot refined product markets remained quiet Tuesday afternoon ahead of the close, though conventional premium gasoline in Houston showed signs of weakening amid solid selling interest, traders said.
In New York Harbor, traders were still waiting for signs that Tosco had come out selling gasoline in a sure signal it had restarted its New Jersey cracker.
Supply concerns engulfed NYMEX amid predictions the American Petroleum Institute (API) would show a solid drop of around 1.5 million barrels last week.
Moments ahead of the close, September gasoline stood 2.11 cents higher at 67.55 cents a gallon, while September heating oil was 0.51 cent higher at 55.60 cents a gallon.
The standoff in New York Harbor gasoline markets continued on Tuesday afternoon, with offers hanging in at firm levels and bidders still hoping to wait for the firmness to go away rather scarce.

"Everyone is on pins and needles waiting to see if someone at Bayway blinks," said one trader, referring resumption of selling by Tosco in connection with the suspected restart of its catalytic cracker at Bayway following unplanned work.
"Even though they're not the biggest player, their absence (as a seller) has caused a lot of focus," the trader said.
Prompt "A2" regular reformulated remained offered at 9.00 cents over September NYMEX, with any month barrels considered doable at 6.00 cents over.
Prompt "M2" regular conventional gasoline was offered at 6.00 cents over and any August was talked at 3.00 cents over.
Gulf markets remained subdued Tuesday afternoon, though plentiful offers on "V1" 93-octane premium were starting to erode regrade values on the grade.
Prompt V1, which was heard done as high as 6.60 over underlying prompt M1 Tuesday morning, was notionally pegged at levels as low as 5.00 cents over M1 -- and possibly lower.
Any month V1 was holding at around 6.00 cent over any month M1, but given the backwardation in M1 markets, any month V1 was still cheaper than the prompt premium barrel.
Prompt back 24th cycle M1 was pegged at about 2.25 cents under, traders said.
-- Oliver Ludwig New York Energy Desk 1 212 859 1633
